newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-STARS OVERSHADOWED BY OLAZABAL COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STARS OVERSHADOWED BY OLAZABAL COMEBACK.

text.p: The world and European number ones, Greg Norman and Colin Montgomerie respectively, are normally the star turns at any golf tournament.
This week they find themselves overshadowed by a player ranked 225th in the world.

Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal, whose talent and exuberance once labelled him a potential threat to both their positions, has chosen the Dubai Desert Classic starting on Thursday for his comeback from 18 months of crippling foot problems.
The Spaniard has spent that time as one of sport's walking wounded, and there were times when he could only crawl to cover the nine feet from his bedroom to his bathroom.

But the player diagnosed three times as suffering from rheumatoid arthritis in both feet was found by a German doctor late last year to be the victim of a bio-mechanical problem, and was put on a regime of physiotherapy and exercise.
Olazabal, ranked ninth before his break, still suffers what he calls "bearable pain" towards the end of rounds and is sensible enough not to set any unrealistic targets for the week.
But he is hoping to play all four rounds which would give him seven for the week including practice, after a prolonged period when he could not complete more than two successive rounds in practice.
"After 18 months of no competition, it would be a little strange to do well," Olazabal said of his prospects.
"My main aim is to test my feet and then assess the situation at the end of the week."
His colleagues have welcomed him back enthusiastically but have agreed that making the halfway cut would be an achievement.

"It is going to be difficult for him to focus and concentrate," said Ryder Cup captain and Spanish colleague Seve Ballesteros, who was impressed by his friend when they played a practice round last week.
"Obviously to play four rounds would be his target now. He has to take it step by step, tournament by tournament."
Montgomerie agreed with Ballesteros on Wednesday. "If he makes the cut it will be a monumental effort but knowing him he'll do it and do quite well.
"He has been a great loss, the European Tour needs him back and it's great to see him back," the Scot added.
While Olazabal's comeback grabs the headlines, Norman is making a return of his own after taking three months off to rest following his fifth Australian Open victory in November.
"I asked Olly out there if he missed it and he said 'Yeah, I missed it, I missed the competition'," Norman said on Wednesday.
"I think that's the same with any athlete, the game gives you competition and it's a challenge every time you play."
Montgomerie is defending the title that he won last year with a shot later designated as the shot of the year on the European Tour.

It was a driver off the fairway that covered 223 yards to clear the lake at the 547-yard final hole, and two putts from 15 feet gave him a birdie four and a one-stroke victory over Miguel Jimenez of Spain.
The world number four's first two outings this year, the Johnnie Walker and Heineken Classics in Australia, brought finishes of 15th and 22nd.
"That's not what I was looking for but it was nothing disastrous and I closed with two 67s," he said.
"It was my putting. At that level if you're not holing out you're not going to win."
He has changed his putter this week and feels comfortable with the new club. "Last year here I didn't miss from six feet or less. If I could do that every week, I'd win every week," he said.
Ian Woosnam and Bernhard Langer are oither big names in the field, along with Italian Costantino Rocca.
